claims.text: In situ high-resolution TEM integrated with EDS/EELS can reveal time-resolved nanoprecipitate composition changes during high-temperature oxidation.
Nanoprecipitates in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 dynamically alter their composition through elemental redistribution during oxidation.
Elemental redistribution from the nanoprecipitates directly affects oxide-scale formation and protective quality.
Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is a dual-nanoprecipitation high-entropy alloy.
The Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy was produced by additive manufacturing.
The additively manufactured alloy exhibits enhanced strength.
The selected alloy has known oxidation-degradation issues.
Oxidation at 700–1100°C in air or controlled atmospheres represents service-relevant conditions for gas-turbine, power-plant, and aerospace applications.
Nanoprecipitates within the HEA matrix serve as reservoirs for reactive elements.
Nanoprecipitates undergo elemental redistribution during oxidation.
At elevated temperatures, the nanoprecipitates partially dissolve or reconfigure.
Nanoprecipitate dissolution or reconfiguration causes localized elemental diffusion and segregation.
Localized diffusion and segregation can promote protective oxides or produce non-protective oxide scales.
Dynamic elemental redistribution modulates the alloy's oxidation resistance.
Elemental migration from nanoprecipitates into growing oxide layers will be observable over time.
Cr and Ti will become locally depleted as they participate in oxide formation.
The extent of nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution will correlate with oxidation kinetics.
Oxidation assessments of cast and wrought counterparts typically rely on post-mortem analyses that cannot capture dynamic elemental redistribution.
The oxidation effects may vary with alloy composition and non-standard testing environments.
